clue.text: They have a quick bite when taking a breather going over hill

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: as in 'as I left', meaning at the time when

indicators.note: to go over something is to turn it over, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a gill is the organ a fish breathes through
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone out walking snatches a quick snack while pausing for breath on the way over a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'breather' sounds like a rest, but here it is the thing that breathes, a fish's gill. 'When' and 'hill' are the outer and last parts, and the turned breather goes after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of the reptiles: crocodilians snap their powerful jaws shut on prey in an instant.

clue.text: Long article about heroin and ecstasy

parts.note: the indefinite article
C is short for circa, Latin for about
H is slang for heroin
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A lengthy newspaper piece covering hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the article, but it is the verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something and to ache for it both mean yearning or wanting it intensely.

clue.text: Ready to attack claim ex is now racist periodically

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these words

explanation.surface: Someone poised to pounce on a former partner's claim that they are no longer a racist.
explanation.walkthrough: Start from the second letter of 'claim' and take every other letter through to the end of 'racist'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to stay hidden in ambush, poised to strike when the target comes along.

clue.text: Nark catching American dons teaching English the second I expressed it's unnecessary

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the quality of being unnecessary

indicators.note: to don clothing is to put it on, so one piece wears another around it

parts.note: a nark and a grass are both slang for a police informer

indicators.note: to catch something is to trap it, so one piece encloses the rest
to express is to press or squeeze out, as juice from fruit, so a letter is forced out

parts.note: tuition is teaching
the second of the two I's in the teaching word goes
US is the abbreviation for American
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An informer snares American academics teaching English, and the speaker declares it pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university teachers, but it is the verb: the American wears the teaching word, after that word loses its second I. A nark is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratuitousness is the quality of being uncalled for or needless, so describing something as having it means it is not required.

clue.text: Contrive to lose a rampant doctor that never leaves the pub

parts.note: to tank a game is to lose it deliberately
taken as written

indicators.note: a rampant heraldic beast rears up on its hind legs, so in a down entry the letters rise and read upwards

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A scheme to get rid of a wild GP who is always propping up the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrive to lose' reads as a plan to shake someone off, but it is one verb: to throw a match. The doctor, rampant, stands on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A pewter or glass beer mug with a handle is a permanent fixture of a pub, often kept behind the bar for regulars.

clue.text: Around tavernas essentially it's drunk neat regularly

definitions.text: Around tavernas essentially it's drunk neat regularly

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters are jumbled
the essence of something is its core, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the word
taken as written

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first and third letters

explanation.surface: Around Greek tavernas this is what people drink, taken straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: a Greek wine served around tavernas and drunk undiluted, while its wordplay mixes letters from three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, the classic drink served in Greek tavernas.

clue.text: That man with £500 set aside

parts.note: the pronoun for that man
the pound sign is L, from Latin libra, and D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A man putting five hundred pounds aside as savings.
explanation.walkthrough: The sum of money splits in two: its symbol and its number each give one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held back is reserved or kept in store, which is what being put to one side means.

clue.text: Boredom reported working a short time in Scotland

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so we want the sound of the words rather than their spelling

parts.words: working a short time in Scotland
parts.note: working is ON, and in Scots a short time is a wee while, or just a wee

explanation.surface: Someone bored while doing a brief stint of work north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Said the French way, ENNUI sounds like ON WEE. Wee is Scottish for small, and a wee is a little while.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loanword for listless weariness and dissatisfaction, a feeling of tedium.

clue.text: Angry complaint about empty parcel delivered to daughter

indicators.note: to be about something is to be around it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a complaint is an illness

indicators.note: an empty thing has lost its contents, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: first and last letters
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An angry protest about an empty package that turned up for a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' suggests grumbling, but here it is a medical complaint, an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being displeased means being annoyed or unhappy with something, a milder form of anger.

clue.text: Love, send D:Ream up to play Things Can Only Get Better

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle with it and move its parts around

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the colon

explanation.surface: A request to get the band D:Ream to perform their hit Things Can Only Get Better.
explanation.walkthrough: D:Ream were a 1990s pop group whose hit Things Can Only Get Better became Labour's 1997 election anthem; the band name is part of the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto means 'never despair', the same hopeful message as the song title.

clue.text: Savage spotted individual laughing in the bush?

definitions.text: Savage spotted individual laughing in the bush?

parts.words: Savage spotted individual laughing in the bush?
parts.note: surface reading: a wild man seen hiding in the undergrowth and cackling
setter's reading: an African animal with a spotted coat famous for its laughing cry, living wild in the bush

explanation.surface: A wild person glimpsed cackling away in the shrubbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' seems to mean seen and 'the bush' a shrub, but they are the animal's coat and the African scrubland.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena of African savanna country is a fierce scavenging predator whose whooping call sounds like laughter.

clue.text: Substances promoting growth in 17 nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and change order

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 17 across

explanation.surface: Growth-promoting substances found in nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like the foods containing the substances, but it is the signal to rearrange, and 'in' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrients are the nourishing compounds in food that living things need to grow and stay healthy.

clue.text: One tears up the road in plum car I'd let out

indicators.note: something out of place is disordered, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy racer in a plum-coloured car, which the speaker lent him, roaring down the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears up the road' suggests reckless speed, but it is literal: breaking up the tarmac. 'In' belongs to the letters, not the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pneumatic drill is a compressed-air jackhammer used by road workers to break up asphalt and concrete surfaces.

clue.text: Disorderly place might calm

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rowdy venue could perhaps be soothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calm' reads as a verb in the surface, but it is the adjective defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A phlegmatic person is unexcitable and composed, staying unruffled under pressure.

clue.text: Lager top drinks Irish broadcaster loved

indicators.note: to drink something is to take it in, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: the frothy top on a glass of beer
RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster

explanation.surface: The foam on a lager soaks up an Irish TV presenter much admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lager top' is the froth on the pint, not a shandy-style drink; RTE (Raidió Teilifís Éireann) slips inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To heart something, in modern informal usage from the heart symbol, is to love it.

clue.text: State courts putting me inside

indicators.note: putting a thing inside places it within, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: atria are open central courts in buildings
colloquially 'us' means me, as in 'give us a hand'

explanation.surface: The state's law courts sending the speaker to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' suggests jail; here it simply places one piece within the other. 'Us' for 'me' is everyday British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a sovereign country in central Europe, and a state is a nation in this sense.

clue.text: Parliamentarian drinks hot beverage after striking head

indicators.note: once the head has been struck off, the first letter is gone

parts.note: a round is drinks bought for a group
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
mead is a drink made from honey

explanation.surface: An MP enjoys a hot drink after a blow to the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parliamentarian' suggests a modern MP, but it means a supporter of Parliament in the English Civil War, whose cropped hair earned the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundheads were the Parliamentarian side fighting King Charles I's Royalists in the 1640s civil war.

clue.text: New PM briefly absorbed by case of Egypt delegate

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in by another, so it goes inside
a case is the outside casing, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters

indicators.note: brief means short, so the word is cut off before its end

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
Liz Truss was UK Prime Minister for seven weeks in 2022

explanation.surface: A new prime minister absorbed in an Egyptian matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New PM briefly' looks like a passing politician, and Liz Truss was famously a new PM only briefly; her name loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrust a task to someone is to hand over responsibility for it, which is what delegating means.

clue.text: In that way the right is supported by Elon, primarily on X

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter
the times sign is read 'by', as in a room six by eight

explanation.surface: A dig at the political right being propped up by Elon Musk's platform X.
explanation.walkthrough: X is not the social network but the multiplication sign; in a down answer, being supported by something means sitting above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby is a formal adverb meaning by that means or as a result of that.

clue.text: Turn round exasperated at first after fellow left without you

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
L is the abbreviation for left
ex is Latin for out of or without, as in ex dividend
U is text speak for you

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first letter
the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone turns round, exasperated, after being abandoned by a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn round' reads as one phrase, but 'Turn' alone is the definition; 'round' gives its first letter and goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexure is a bend or curve, the act of bending or flexing, so a turn in that sense.

clue.text: Split force is no problem

parts.note: F is the symbol for force in physics
taken as written
'sure' is a casual reply meaning no problem

explanation.surface: Breaking something apart by force is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as a verb in the surface, but it is a noun: the crack itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A fissure is a long narrow crack or opening, as in rock, which is a split.

clue.text: Gets wrong motorway to northern city — learner is stumped by satnav initially

indicators.note: being stumped means being got out and replaced at the crease, so one letter makes way for another

parts.note: the M1 motorway, with the 1 read as I
Sunderland is a city in north-east England
L for learner, as on L-plates; this letter goes out
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped; these letters come in

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A learner driver takes the wrong motorway to a northern city, baffled by the satnav.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is England's main north-south motorway. In cricket a batter out stumped is recorded as 'st' on the scorecard; here those letters take the learner's place in SUNDERLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: To misunderstand something is to grasp its meaning incorrectly, which is getting it wrong.

clue.text: Conscientious objector punches Parisian on hunt

indicators.note: a punch goes into something, so one piece is driven inside another

parts.note: sur is French for on
CO is the abbreviation for conscientious objector

explanation.surface: A pacifist lashes out at a Frenchman out hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian on' asks for the French word for 'on'; the pacifist's abbreviation sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour an area is to search it thoroughly and rapidly, which is to hunt through it.

clue.text: Almost perfect aim

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost perfect aim' sounds like a near miss at a target; 'aim' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can mean an intention or plan, as in 'the idea is to finish early', which is an aim.

clue.text: Union member's paraphernalia ultimately upset polymath

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter
Jean-Jacques Rousseau was a philosopher, writer and composer

explanation.surface: A trade unionist's kit eventually upsets a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union member' suggests a trade unionist, but the union is a marriage and the member a bride.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride collects for her marriage, so a newlywed's belongings.

clue.text: Feel apprehensive about duke on a date

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
AD, anno Domini, is attached to a year

explanation.surface: Nerves before a date with an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the start of the wordplay, but it ends the definition; 'on' is the piece meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to anticipate it with fear or great unease, which is to feel apprehensive.

clue.text: Find fault with swimmer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to complain or nag pettily

explanation.surface: Criticising someone's swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person in a pool, but it is a fish; 'with' only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for petty grumbling and the name of a common freshwater fish.

clue.text: Interactive software really excited news providers

parts.note: hyper means overexcited
the media are the press and broadcasters

explanation.surface: Journalists getting very worked up about new interactive computer programs.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit in the order of the clue, with no indicators needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypermedia are linked multimedia systems in which users click through text, images and sound, like the web.
